questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has side lengths 5, 5, and 8. How is it classified by sides?

feedback.text: Scalene means no side lengths match.
Two sides match, so the triangle is isosceles.
Equilateral requires all three side lengths to match.
Right classifies by angles, not side lengths.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has side lengths 4, 6, and 9. How is it classified by sides?

feedback.text: Isosceles requires at least two congruent sides.
Equilateral requires three congruent sides.
Obtuse classifies by angles, not side lengths.
All three side lengths are different, so the triangle is scalene.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has side lengths 7, 7, and 7. How is it classified by sides?

feedback.text: All three sides are congruent, so the triangle is equilateral.
Equilateral triangles are isosceles too, but the most precise classification is equilateral.
Scalene means no congruent sides.
Right classification needs angle evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has angles 35°, 55°, and 90°. How is it classified by angles?

feedback.text: Acute requires all angles less than 90°.
Obtuse requires one angle greater than 90°.
One angle is exactly 90°, so the triangle is right.
Equilateral is a side classification and would have three 60° angles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has angles 40°, 65°, and 75°. How is it classified by angles?

feedback.text: A right triangle needs one 90° angle.
All angles are less than 90°, so the triangle is acute.
An obtuse triangle needs one angle greater than 90°.
Scalene classifies side lengths, not angles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has angles 25°, 35°, and 120°. How is it classified by angles?

feedback.text: One angle is greater than 90°, so the triangle is obtuse.
Acute requires all angles less than 90°.
Right requires one angle exactly 90°.
Isosceles classifies side lengths.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

Which evidence is enough to classify a triangle as equilateral?

feedback.text: Appearance is not evidence for equilateral classification.
Two equal-looking angles do not prove all sides congruent.
A 90° angle identifies a right triangle, not an equilateral triangle.

answer.text: All three sides have matching congruence marks.

feedback.text: Three matching side marks show all sides are congruent.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

Which phrase uses precise triangle notation?

answer.text: The triangle is kind of pointy.

feedback.text: This is informal and not mathematical.
This is vague and unsupported.
This names the triangle and gives precise classifications.
This relies on appearance and unclear language.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has all three sides congruent. What must also be true?

feedback.text: Three congruent sides define an equilateral triangle.
Scalene means no sides are congruent.
Equilateral triangles have 60° angles, not an obtuse angle.
An equilateral triangle cannot have a right angle.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has exactly two sides marked congruent and one angle marked 100°. Which classification is supported?

feedback.text: The side marks show isosceles, not scalene, and 100° is not acute.
Equilateral would require three congruent sides and three 60° angles.
A right triangle needs a 90° angle.
Two congruent sides make it isosceles, and 100° makes it obtuse.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has side lengths 6, 8, and 10 and one angle marked 90°. Which classification is supported?

feedback.text: Isosceles would require two equal side lengths.
All side lengths differ and one angle is 90°.
Equilateral triangles cannot have a right angle.
A 90° angle makes it right, not obtuse.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has angles 60°, 60°, and 60°. Which angle classification is correct?

feedback.text: No angle is 90°.
No angle is greater than 90°.
Each angle is less than 90°, so the triangle is acute.
Scalene is a side classification.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

Which statement is supported by two matching side tick marks?

answer.text: The triangle has three congruent sides.

feedback.text: Three congruent sides would need three matching side marks.
Side tick marks do not prove a 90° angle.
Side tick marks do not prove an obtuse angle.

answer.text: The triangle has at least two congruent sides.

feedback.text: Two matching side marks support at least two congruent sides.

Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has no matching side marks and side lengths 3, 4, and 5. What side classification is supported?

feedback.text: The side lengths are all different, so it is scalene.
Isosceles requires two equal side lengths.
Equilateral requires all three sides equal.
Acute requires angle information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

Which classification uses angle measures only?

feedback.text: Equilateral describes side lengths.
Isosceles describes side lengths.
Obtuse describes a triangle with one angle greater than 90°.
Scalene describes side lengths.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

Which classification uses side lengths only?

feedback.text: Right describes angle measure.
Scalene describes a triangle with no congruent sides.
Acute describes angle measure.
Obtuse describes angle measure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has side lengths 9, 9, and 12. Which side classification is most precise?

feedback.text: Equilateral requires three equal sides.
Scalene requires no equal sides.
Exactly two side lengths match, so isosceles is most precise.
Right cannot be determined from these side labels alone in this readiness item.

Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

feedback.text: All three angles are less than 90°.

No angle is greater than 90°.

Question ID: GEO_U03_L01_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.2 (readiness support)

A triangle has one angle labeled 91°. What angle classification is already determined?

feedback.text: Right requires exactly 90°.

Equiangular would require all angles congruent.
One angle greater than 90° makes the triangle obtuse.

answer.text: All three sides have matching tick marks.

feedback.text: Matching tick marks support equilateral classification.
